reply.summary: Rewrote docs/designs/016-harness-evidence-and-read-rights/01-research.md for ADR-016, this time staying fully independent: no reads, greps, globs, or shells touched any run's transcripts/ or reviews/ records (the previous attempt's gate failure). Findings are grounded in the source ADR, the shipped harness (gates.ts stdio:'ignore' booleans and CARGO_GATE legs; independence.ts read/write asymmetry and reportKey identity machinery; state-store.ts additive-optional grammar and 8MiB cap; prompts.ts 'not exposed by endpoint' parameters default; opencode-runner.ts tokens/cost already on the SDK reply; flows/cli planMaxLines and --max-parallel=1), the .opencode agent permission configs, and verified external primary sources (OpenCode permissions docs, llama.cpp server README flags, GitHub Actions 1MiB step-summary cap, Claude Code sandboxing protected paths, Rust Book test-result line). Lenses applied: Prior art, Security landscape, Performance baselines. Every factual claim carries an inline source; unverifiable ADR operator numbers are flagged as operator-observed, and eight open questions are handed to the designer.
reply.commitMessage: docs: research harness evidence and read rights for ADR-016
docs: add design proposal for ADR-016 harness evidence and read rights

findings.location: Chosen design §3, "Document families" bullet vs "Run-record block" bullet — "then trailing denies: `*transcripts*` and `*reviews*` over shell, `glob` and `grep` rules over `docs/designs/**/transcripts/**`" vs the block "appended last to every shell-holding agent (… the five document families)" with "`glob` denies over `docs/designs/**/transcripts/**` and `docs/designs/**/reviews/**`; `grep` denies `*transcripts*` and `*reviews*`"
findings.problem: The document families are specified with two different run-record rule sets: the first bullet scopes their glob/grep denies to transcripts/ only, the second appends denies over reviews/** as well. A grep rule keyed to the path-shaped resource docs/designs/**/transcripts/** can never match under the proposal's own A17 semantics (grep resources are the requested regex, not the search path), so it is a dead rule; and if the transcripts-only reading governs, ADR Decision 3's clause "`glob`/`grep` pattern rules for the same directories" (both transcripts/ and reviews/) is under-delivered for the document families.
findings.fix: Make the run-record block the single authority for the doc families' run-record denies — drop the narrower glob/grep clause from the first bullet, keeping its note that the read route to handed reports stays open — so one rule set per agent is specified.

findings.location: Chosen design §3, "Document families" bullet — "(`cd`, `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep`, `rg`, `find`, `git status *`, `git diff *`, `git log *`, `git show *`)"
findings.problem: Under the permission grammar the proposal itself relies on (A16/A17; whole-value matching where only a rule ending in ` *` additionally matches the bare command), bare resources like `cat` and `wc` match only argument-less commands, so every useful inspection command (`wc <file>`, `cat <path>`) stays denied behind the kept leading `shell * → deny`. As written the widening buys nothing and defeats Decision 3's purpose ("so a proposal can check a path and a line count"). The git entries carry stars; the rest do not — an inconsistency in exactly the rule text an implementer copies.
findings.fix: Spell every entry in star form (`cat *`, `ls *`, `wc *`, `find *`, `cd *`, …) or state "byte-identical to the inspection set already shipped in `code/coder.md`" as the design-panel bullet does; pin with-argument commands (`wc <file>` allowed) in Test strategy #4 instead of bare names.

findings.location: Chosen design §1, "Prompts" bullet — "the report at `{{reportPath}}` is yours — re-reading it is allowed" while "seat agents' `read` deny over `docs/designs/**/reviews/**` (A10) stays"
findings.problem: The seat's only reachable re-read route is `git diff`, and for a report written this attempt and not yet committed, `git diff <untracked>` prints nothing; the prompt invites the seat to try the permission-denied `read` tool first and burn a turn on a dead route — the friction class ADR-016 exists to stop.
findings.fix: One clause naming the route and its audit-level meaning, e.g. "re-reading it is allowed (via your `git diff` allow — your `read` tool stays fenced off `reviews/`)".

findings.location: Chosen design §4, "Document ceiling" bullet — "above the observed shipped artifacts (this run's `01-research.md` is 440 lines; the 012 proposal ~505)"
findings.problem: These run-artifact line counts are stated as fact but appear in no assumption-register row, unlike every other operator-observed number (A19/A20 register that class explicitly); the 600-line cap's headroom rests entirely on them, and a miscount above 600 turns every normal full-flow run red at a document stage.
findings.fix: Add one unverified register row for the current artifact sizes behind the 600 cap, or drop the specific counts and cite fixture evidence.

findings.location: Chosen design §3 — "Run-record block, appended last to every shell-holding agent" vs next bullet "Own-report re-open, per seat agent after the deny"
findings.problem: The own-report re-open must come after the block for last-match-wins to work, so the block is not actually appended last; the two bullets state contradictory orderings.
findings.fix: Reword to "appended after all other rules except the per-seat own-report re-open".

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| macOS | unknown | Nothing platform-specific is added (pipe capture and `spawn` are portable Node), but no environment here exercises it |" and "| Windows / WSL2 | unknown | Same posture as macOS |"
findings.problem: The checklist treats an `unknown` matrix status as a major finding, and the rows' justification is contradicted by §3: doc families gain a POSIX-only inspection set ("append the inspection set (`cd`, `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep`, `rg`, `find`, …)") and the design panel gains spawned cargo/rustfmt/npm legs. Both are platform-dependent tool surfaces, so "nothing platform-specific is added" overstates portability instead of justifying the abstraction.
findings.fix: Replace `unknown` in both rows with a declared posture ("not exercised — harness change developed and tested on Linux only") and add one sentence naming the two platform-dependent additions (POSIX inspection set, cargo/npm check legs) as the reason no claim is made. Document-only.

findings.location: §1 Own-report identity — "a `reviews/` access value is the seat's own report iff `reportKey(value)` (everything from the `reviews` segment on) equals `reportKey(opts.ownReportPath)`"
findings.problem: The identity rule, §3's `glob` denies over `docs/designs/**/reviews/**`, and the per-seat shell allow all key on `/`-separated, case-exact path spelling, and no assumption row (A2, A16, A17) states that access values or shell command text reach the audit separator-normalized. Where paths are spelled with `\` or differ in case, the deny side fails safe but the own-report exemption silently never fires, so Decision 1's promise is unmet on that host while the matrix claims nothing platform-specific changes.
findings.fix: Add one clause to the identity rule: `reportKey` compares after normalizing separators to `/` and case — or, if the SDK already normalizes, add an assumption row stating that with where it was verified.

findings.location: §3 Read-only reach — "`shell git diff *reviews/<phase>/<specialty>-*` → allow, naming the agent's own specialty in the pattern (A11)"
findings.problem: The deny-then-reallow order depends entirely on OpenCode's matcher grammar (`*` spans `/`, a rule ending ` *` matches the bare command, last match wins), and A16 says the pin is "a repo-local re-implementation of OpenCode's wildcard matching". The matrix row "Pre-ADR-016 OpenCode server config | yes | Only standard rule types … are used" vouches for rule types, not for that grammar, so drift in the engine silently inverts the whole §3 deny stack.
findings.fix: Name the OpenCode version whose documented grammar the rules rely on in one assumption row and in that matrix row's note, and state in Test strategy #4 that the repo-local matcher stays pinned to that version.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| A run in flight across the merge | yes | Pre-016 checkpoint ⇒ `gateEvidence` absent ⇒ prompts render \"(no gate record for this run yet)\" |"
findings.problem: The row claims a flat `yes` but accounts only for the checkpoint and transcript effects. The same merge applies `docMaxLines: 600` and `research` in `docStages` to a resumed run, and the Risks table itself says "A resumed or in-flight run meets the new `docMaxLines`: a document already over 600 fails its next document stage". The matrix understates a behavior change across the merge.
findings.fix: Extend that row with the condition: "…; a document already over `docMaxLines` fails its next document stage — raise the cap or force the stage (Risks)", keeping the status.

findings.location: §2 The gate record — "`tail` the last `MAX_GATE_TAIL_BYTES = 2_000` bytes of the leg's merged stdout+stderr, passed through `printable` (independence.ts:311) before storage"
findings.problem: The bound is in bytes over raw child output, so the slice can cut a multi-byte code point, and cargo/npm output under a non-UTF-8 console codepage (the Windows row) is not UTF-8 at all; that string is persisted in the checkpoint and rendered into four prompts and the build note. The Risks row about the rolling tail covers only truncation of the `test result:` line, so "tails are evidence, not parsed contracts" does not cover mojibake reaching five seats.
findings.fix: One clause: capture bytes, decode once as UTF-8 with replacement, then bound the tail in characters against the same `2_000` budget — or state explicitly that a tail's head may drop a partial code point and who strips it.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix, Linux row — "all changes are Node ≥ 22.23.4 in `tools/orchestration`, agent-config YAML text, and prompt text"
findings.problem: The Node floor is asserted with no anchor (no engines reference, no assumption row), so the checklist's Node-floor check cannot be verified from the document; and §3 edits `.md` agent rule files ("Config edits in `.opencode/agents/`, using the rule text already shipped in `code/coder.md`"), not "YAML".
findings.fix: Cite the declared floor's source (the package's engines field) and write "agent rule text in `.opencode/agents/`" instead of "agent-config YAML text".

findings.location: Chosen design §1 Own-report identity on the audit's read side — "a `reviews/` access value is the seat's own report iff `reportKey(value)` (everything from the `reviews` segment on) equals `reportKey(opts.ownReportPath)`"
findings.problem: Keying from the `reviews` segment on drops the design-directory prefix, but every run shares the report grammar `reviews/<phase>/<specialty>-rN[cM].md` (A11), so a seat's own key is identical to the same-named report under every other design directory. Reads of another run's reports — a violation today — would pass the exemption silently, contradicting ADR Decision 1's clause "Every other `reviews/` path stays a violation" and letting a panel anchor on prior runs' verdicts. The §3 per-seat allow `git diff *reviews/design/<specialty>-*` opens the same cross-run paths (A16: `*` spans `/`), so both the permission layer and the audit open and no backstop fails it; the Risks seam row covers only same-run prior rounds.
findings.fix: Scope the identity to the run before comparing keys: canonicalize the access value and require it to lie under the attempt's design directory (the directory of `opts.ownReportPath`) — i.e. compare canonicalized full paths against `ownReportPath`, which keeps the ADR's absolute-vs-repo-relative spelling equivalence while rejecting a foreign design dir's same-named report. Apply the same containment to the shell branch's REVIEWS_KEY matches; extend Test strategy #3 with a cross-design-directory same-name read fixture that must fail the audit.

findings.location: Chosen design §2 The gate record — "the block is the runner's own record and its failing-leg tail belongs, verbatim, in the `03-build-notes.md` 'Gate posture' section"
findings.problem: The tail is merged stdout+stderr of the very code the run writes and fixes; a stage can plant text in its test output (2,000 bytes is ample for an instruction line) that then reaches all five review seats and the fix loop fenced and labeled as the runner's own record, with a mandate to quote it verbatim into the committed build note. The proposal never classifies this data source (security checklist item 1), while §1/§3 exist to close exactly this stage-to-seat anchoring channel.
findings.fix: Fix provenance in one sentence rendered in the block header and the prompt: the tails are output the runner captured from the code under review — citable evidence, not instructions — and replace "verbatim" with "cited with the leg command and exit" for the build note. No new mechanism; does not touch the ADR's decision that the record is shared ground truth.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix, Linux row — "all changes are Node ≥ 22.23.4 in `tools/orchestration`"
findings.problem: Node 22.23.4 carries the HIGH-severity CVEs of the 2026-11-11 Node.js security release (CVE-2026-123864, -123865, -123866, -123872; all 22.x < 22.23.5 affected), fixed in 22.23.5 published two days before this review. A named dependency with a known advisory must be addressed (checklist item 5).
findings.fix: Raise the stated floor to Node ≥ 22.23.5 in the compatibility-matrix row and the package `engines` pin — one-line change.

findings.location: Chosen design §2 capture shape — "`tail` the last `MAX_GATE_TAIL_BYTES = 2_000` bytes of the leg's merged stdout+stderr, passed through `printable`"
findings.problem: Checklist item 4 unaddressed: the design never states what a leg tail may carry (absolute local paths, env echoes, failing-npm error lines that can embed registry URLs and credential-bearing text), where it persists (checkpoint, transcripts, five prompts), or what is committed once the verbatim tail lands in `03-build-notes.md` in an open-source repo.
findings.fix: State the posture in §2: extend the `printable` pass with a redaction step (known token patterns, home-directory paths) before storage, or declare the record local-only and require the scrub before build-note insertion.

findings.location: §4 Budgeted, measured context — "and states a ceiling: at most 25 reads of files outside that set."
findings.problem: The ceiling bounds the count of reads but not their size. Unlike every other constant in the design (600 derived from the observed 440/505-line artifacts and the 2,696-line runaway; 2,000/6,000 pinned against the 8 MiB checkpoint and the 189,788-token prompt baseline), 25 is stated without derivation. Prior-run artifacts are not size-capped by this design (run 2's 2,696-line proposal is still on disk), so the worst case of 25 large out-of-set reads plausibly re-creates the large research prompt Decision 4 exists to measure, and it exceeds what A20's 32,768-token resident KV can hold — a gap between the design's numbers and the research baseline without explanation (performance checklist item 6).
findings.fix: One sentence deriving 25 against the ADR's numbers: the estimated worst-case token cost of 25 out-of-set reads versus the 189,788-token largest-prompt / 32,768-resident-prefix figures — or state that the ceiling's worst case assumes out-of-set documents under docMaxLines. No mechanism change.

findings.location: §2 The gate record — "GateEvidence = { at: number; green: boolean; legs: GateLeg[] }"
findings.problem: The record carries `at` but nothing renders or checks it, and the design never states the record's freshness rule: a seat reading the block cannot tell which diff a tail belongs to. Invalidation is overwrite-at-each-gate-call, which is correct by construction (only the gated implement/fix/test-update stages change code; the resumed pre-016 case renders the absent-record line), but that correspondence — invalidation being correct, not just fast — is left implicit (checklist item 5).
findings.fix: One sentence at the runner bullet: the gate call replaces state.gateEvidence wholesale, so a rendered block always describes the gate over the current state; `at` is for forensics only. Or render `at` into the block header.

findings.location: Chosen design §3, document-family bullet — "then trailing denies: `*transcripts*` and `*reviews*` over shell, `glob` and `grep` rules over `docs/designs/**/transcripts/**`"
findings.problem: This inline deny list overlaps but does not match the 'Run-record block, appended last to every shell-holding agent (... the five document families)', which also covers the doc families but additionally denies glob over `docs/designs/**/reviews/**` and denies grep of `*transcripts*`/`*reviews*` rather than path-scoped grep rules. Two overlapping, differently-worded rule lists for the same agents leave the implementer to choose which wins, and duplicated rule text drifts — §3 elsewhere holds rule text to byte-identical reuse. (new)
findings.fix: End the document-family bullet with '...then the run-record block below' and delete its inline trailing-deny clause, making the run-record block the single statement of the denies; this removes text rather than adding any.

findings.location: Chosen design §2 — "Canonical shape, defined once here: `GateEvidence = { at: number; green: boolean; legs: GateLeg[] }`"
findings.problem: `at` has no stated consumer: the `gateEvidenceText` spec, the build-note sentence, and the test strategy never reference it. Every other field traces to a named use; this one is record weight with no reader (checklist #6's consumer-less knob applied to a record field). (new)
findings.fix: Drop the field, or state its one consumer in a clause — e.g. `gateEvidenceText` prints `at` as a 'gate run at' header line, which also disambiguates the evidence in a multi-attempt run.

reply.summary: All six majors were consumed by changing the design, mostly by deletion: correctness #1 — the doc-families bullet's narrower transcripts-only glob/grep clause is deleted so the run-record block is the single rule set; correctness #2 — the hand-written inspection list is deleted in favour of "byte-identical to `code/coder.md`'s star-form rules", with Test strategy #4 now pinning `wc <file>`/`cat <path>`; compatibility #1 — both `unknown` matrix rows replaced by `not exercised` postures naming the POSIX inspection set and the cargo/npm legs; security #1 — the own-report identity now canonicalizes the access value (A17's `/`- and case-normalization, newly registered on the live V2 permissions page) and requires containment in the attempt's design directory, in both the read and shell branches, with Test strategy #3's cross-design-directory fixture and the Risks seam row extended to cover it; security #2 — the rendered block carries a provenance header (runner-captured output from the code under review, never instructions) and "verbatim" is replaced by citing the tail with its leg command and exit; security #3 — the stated floor rises to Node ≥ 22.23.5 in the matrix row plus a Rollout line for the `engines.node` change. The minors/nits are handled in the same passages: prompt names the `git diff` re-read route, run-record block ordering, printable-at-write-and-render placement, character-bounded UTF-8 decode of the tail, in-flight-run `docMaxLines` condition, engines-field citation, matcher-grammar pin (A16/#4); the doc-ceiling minor forced a measurement — the body's unregistered counts were wrong and a 600 cap sits below shipped artifacts (014's 733-line proposal), so the sizes are registered as verified A24 and the cap rises to 900. Deletions balance the additions: the duplicate run-record rule set, the §3 subagent restatement, §1's child-walk bullet, the worktree/Non-goals duplication, and the read-ceiling Non-goals bullet are gone, and the Revision log replaced its r0 placeholder with six two-line entries. The diff is +13 lines net because five majors each required a clause the document did not previously state (directory-scoped identity, provenance header, decoded character bound, declared non-Linux posture, raised engines floor) and a measured cap value had to be registered; nothing was added that an existing passage already said.
reply.commitMessage: docs: scope own-report identity to the run, fix gate-tail provenance and platform posture in the ADR-016 proposal

findings.location: Chosen design §1, shell branch — "collect every `REVIEWS_KEY` match in the command; if the set is non-empty and every match canonicalizes, under the rule above, to `own`, exempt" combined with the identity rule's "resolved against the repo root — lies under the attempt's own design directory"
findings.problem: new: the canonicalization input is ambiguous and both readings have a defect. If the REVIEWS_KEY match itself (a span starting at `reviews/`) is canonicalized, resolving it against the repo root never lands under the attempt's design directory, so under that literal reading no shell access is ever exempt — contradicting Test #3's "shell `git diff <own>` is clean". Under the sensible reading (canonicalize the full path token), the legitimate relative spelling the per-seat permission wildcard itself allows — `cd docs/designs/<dir> && git diff reviews/design/<specialty>-r1c1.md`, since A16's `*` matches zero characters and the inspection set allows `cd *` — resolves to `<repo>/reviews/...`, fails the new directory test, and loses the exemption it had under the pre-revision `reportKey(value) === own` rule: a regression in exactly the friction class Decision 1 removes.
findings.fix: Canonicalize the full path token the match sits in, and apply the design-directory test only to values that spell a design directory — bare `reviews/...` spans pass on reportKey equality alone; add the cd-relative `git diff <own>` spelling to Test strategy #3's clean set.

findings.location: Chosen design §1 identity rule — "normalized the way the permission layer normalizes paths (A17: `\` to `/`, case folded)"
findings.problem: new: the gloss over-attributes A17's authority. A17 and the cited permissions page make case-insensitive matching Windows-only, so "the way the permission layer normalizes paths" on Linux (the only exercised host) does not case-fold — yet Test #3 expects case-variant spellings of own report to pass the exemption, so the audit must fold case unconditionally by its own rule, a deliberate superset of both the permission layer's Linux normalization and ADR Decision 1's exact "identity match on the report key". Unreachable through the permission layer on Linux (the `reviews/**` read deny is segment-exact), so no exploitable over-exemption — but the citation claims support the rule does not actually receive.
findings.fix: State that the audit's canonicalization folds case on every platform as its own rule (citing A17 only for the `\`→`/` normalization), or drop "case folded" from the rule and the case-variant spellings from Test #3.

findings.location: Chosen design §3 Read-only reach — "then the inspection set byte-for-byte as `code/coder.md` ships it — star form throughout"
findings.problem: new: The inherited read-only set was enumerated inside the document in r0 (matching ADR-016 Decision 3's named commands); the revision defines it only by reference to code/coder.md. ADR Decision 3 names four read commands (git status, git diff, git log, git show) besides the file readers, and Test strategy #4 simultaneously narrowed its pin from r0's "doc families allow `cat`/`wc`/`git status`" to "doc families allow `wc <file>` and `cat <path>`" — so neither the document nor its tests pin that the referenced coder.md set contains the ADR's git read commands, and drift in coder.md would silently shrink the doc families' ADR-mandated reach; the matrix's own macOS/Windows rows cite "§3's inspection set" as the host-dependent surface, which is now un-enumerable from the document. Fix replaces the dropped r0 enumeration rather than adding a mechanism.
findings.fix: One clause (or one assumption row with coder.md line refs, as A8 provides) stating coder.md's inspection set is exactly ADR-016 Decision 3's read-only set in star form, and extend Test #4's pin to the `git status *`/`git diff *`/`git log *`/`git show *` allows for doc families.

findings.location: Chosen design §1 Own-report identity, shell branch — "collect every `REVIEWS_KEY` match in the command; if the set is non-empty and every match canonicalizes, under the rule above, to `own`, exempt"
findings.problem: The containment test r1 asked for has no defined operand on the shell route, so the cross-run read is not closed by determinate text. The rule tests a "canonical spelling … resolved against the repo root" for lying under the attempt's design directory, but the operand the shell bullet hands it is the REVIEWS_KEY match, which by the design's own definition (A2, §1's "everything from the `reviews` segment on") has the design-directory prefix stripped. A prefix-less fragment (`reviews/design/security-r1c1.md`) resolved against the repo root can never lie under `docs/designs/<run>/`, so either (a) the exemption never fires on the shell route — the only route a seat can use to re-read its own report (A21; §1's new prompt sentence says re-reading is allowed "through your `git diff*` allow") — so Decision 1 does not take effect and Test strategy #11 fails; or (b) the implementer restores it by resolving the fragment against the attempt's own design directory, which makes containment vacuously true and reopens the hole: `git diff docs/designs/014-<…>/reviews/design/security-r1.md` yields the same fragment as the seat's own key and passes the exemption. Prior runs' `reviews/` trees are committed in this repo, the per-seat wildcard already opens those paths at the permission layer, and the Risks seam row concedes that reach, so the audit's identity rule is the only backstop — and it is the ambiguous text. Re-raised: the r1 revision states the right intent but does not name the string that carries the discriminating prefix.
findings.fix: Name the compared operand once in §1's shell bullet: take the whole path token in the command leg that contains the `reviews` segment, canonicalize it against the repo root, require it to lie under the attempt's design directory, and only then compare `reportKey`; state that a match with no design-directory prefix is not an identity match (fails closed). Add to Test strategy #3 the two spellings §3's allow actually opens: `git diff docs/designs/<own>/reviews/design/<specialty>-r1c1.md` clean, `git diff docs/designs/<other-run>/reviews/design/<specialty>-r1c1.md` fails. No new mechanism.

findings.location: Risks tail row ("no redaction pass ships and no whole tail is published") vs Chosen design §2 build-note sentence ("a failing-leg tail belongs in the `03-build-notes.md` 'Gate posture' section cited with its leg command and exit")
findings.problem: The rebuttal's premise contradicts the §2 sentence it answers: 03-build-notes.md is a committed artifact in this open repo and §2 mandates tail content land there, so tail content is published, just selectively. The same row concedes a tail "can carry absolute paths or registry text" — checklist item 4's boundary, since a failing `npm run check` line can embed a credential-bearing registry URL and a test can echo environment variables — yet nothing states what must be dropped before the citation is committed, and the design never says where the record persists (checkpoint/transcripts local, build note committed). The decision to ship no redaction pass is sound and is not re-argued; only the claimed coverage is wrong.
findings.fix: One clause on §2's build-note sentence: the citation is line-selective and drops any line carrying a credential-bearing token or an absolute local path — the posture the Risks row already claims — and name in that row which artifacts are committed. No redaction pass added.

reply.summary: Major (r1c1 shell-branch identity): §1's shell bullet now names the compared operand — whole command tokens containing the `reviews` segment, prefix included, explicitly never the prefix-stripped REVIEWS_KEY fragment — exempted only via the §1 identity rule, with a prefix-less token stated to resolve outside the attempt's design directory and fail closed; Test strategy #3 pins the two spellings §3's allow opens (own design-dir path clean, same path under another run fails). Minor (Risks row vs §2): the contradictory 'no whole tail is published' claim is deleted — the Risks row now names the checkpoint and transcripts as local and the committed build note as the one carrier, and §2's build-note sentence states the citation is line-selective, dropping credential-bearing and absolute-path lines. Offsetting trims: Context's exclusions tail (dup of Non-goals) and the research-ceiling parenthetical (dup of Deferred) were removed; Revision log's §1 and §2 entries superseded in place with r2 wording. Net line change is zero (450 → 450).
reply.commitMessage: docs: fix own-report shell operand and build-note citation scope in ADR-016 proposal

findings.location: Chosen design §1 shell branch + Test strategy #3 — "a prefix-less token resolves outside the attempt's design directory and fails closed"
findings.problem: new: The r2 revision's fail-closed half — a prefix-less shell spelling of the own report (e.g. `git diff reviews/design/<specialty>-r1c1.md`), which §3's `*`-prefixed wildcard allow does let through the permission layer so the audit is the only thing that can stop it — is asserted in the rule text and the Revision log but has no fixture. Test strategy #3 pins the clean own-spelling and the cross-run/sibling failures but not this spelling.
findings.fix: Add one assertion to Test strategy #3: the prefix-less shell spelling fails the audit even though §3's wildcard permits it at the permission layer. No new mechanism.

findings.location: Chosen design §1, shell branch — "a prefix-less token resolves outside the attempt's design directory and fails closed"
findings.problem: new (surviving half of my r1 minor, re-raised): the fail-closed clause this revision adds is reachable through rules the same document ships, and is neither pinned nor enumerated. §3's per-seat re-open `shell git diff *reviews/design/<specialty>-*` matches, under A16's grammar, with the leading `*` spanning the empty prefix, and §3's inspection set (byte-for-byte `code/coder.md`, ADR Decision 3's `cd`) permits `cd docs/designs/<dir> && git diff reviews/design/<specialty>-r1c1.md` — so the permission layer admits a command the audit then fails, while §3 asserts prompt, permission layer, and audit "say the same thing". The Risks seam row enumerates only "the seat's prior-round reports and another design directory's same-named report", and §3's seam sentence only "prior-round and other runs' same-named reports", so the one own-report spelling the allow admits and §1 rejects is described nowhere, and Test strategy #3 pins neither direction of it. findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:3133-3147 (citableCwd), against the repo idiom at runner.ts:222 / identity.ts:59 / moves.ts:175
findings.problem: Checklist item 3: the new relativization is hand-rolled string manipulation (`split('\\').join('/')`, `startsWith(root + '/')`, `slice`) rather than the shipped `relative(repoDir, target)` idiom. The comparison is case-sensitive, so on the case-insensitive hosts whose absolute-path spelling the code explicitly handles (`C:\Work\…` vs `c:\work\…`) it falls through to `'(cwd withheld)'` and every leg's package dir silently disappears from the committed record — where `path.win32.relative` would be case-insensitive. Linux, the only exercised platform, derives the dirs from `join(repoDir, …)`, so the match is guaranteed there.
findings.fix: Use `relative(repoDir, cwd).split(/[\\/]/).join('/')` and keep `'(cwd withheld)'` only when the result escapes the root (a `..` segment).

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:3192-3194 (greenSummary slice), against boundedTail's stated rule in tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/gates.ts:323-370
findings.problem: Checklist item 5: the citable clause is cut with `tail.slice(at, stop)`, i.e. by UTF-16 units, while boundedTail in the same feature was written to bound by code points explicitly because "slicing units can cut a surrogate pair". A 160-unit window ending inside a surrogate pair (non-BMP character in a test name or path) puts a lone surrogate into the rendered evidence block: printable runs at write, before the slice, and neither defuseFences nor the cap re-sanitizes it.
findings.fix: Slice code points (`Array.from(tail).slice(a, b).join('')`) as boundedTail does, or re-apply the code-point guard after slicing.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/gates.ts:366; tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:3090-3105
findings.problem: boundedTail concatenates the tail-cap elision note directly onto the kept span with no separator, so when the kept span begins exactly at a line-initial absolute path (rustc/cargo emit such lines), the line the citation rule sees starts `[…]` followed by `/home/...`; the POSIX branch of ABSOLUTE_PATH_LINE is anchored (`^` or `[\s'"(=,]` must precede the slash), so the glue hides it and one absolute host path survives into the committed checkpoint and prompts. Credential patterns are unanchored and unaffected; this is host-layout disclosure only. The dirty fixture uses short tails, so it never exercises the glue.
findings.fix: Separate the boundedTail note from the kept span with a newline (or strip a leading elision note in citableTail before judging each line / add `]` to ABSOLUTE_PATH_LINE's leading class), and extend the dirty fixture with a >MAX_GATE_TAIL_CHARS output whose cut lands at a line-initial absolute path, asserting it does not reach the persisted record.
